claims.statement: The fragment selects a policy under Repository creation without defining the options or inheritance. A UI choice is not a saved restriction, observed creation denial or authority to create repositories.

Selecting one or more repository types is conditional on first choosing Members can create repositories. The fragment does not enumerate allowed types or imply every visibility is permitted, nor does it verify effective member entitlement.
The repositories-named fragment actually navigates to Member privileges under Policies. It is not a repository listing, complete estate census, role grant or verified policy value.

The fragment selects a policy from Repository deletion and transfer. It does not specify policy options, actor roles, bypasses, recoverability or actual deletion/transfer behavior, and is not authority to perform destructive operations.

The fragment points to the product-variable security-and-quality tab at the page top. It does not show controls, evidence of scans, enabled security enforcement or a validated product-specific rendered menu; no security setting changed.

The fragment locates Custom properties in the sidebar. It supplies no property schema, requiredness, effective repository values, policy binding or verified metadata coverage; no custom property was set.
